# Idle Buddy

> A macOS desktop mascot widget that appears when a Claude Code or Codex task runs
> longer than 30 seconds, suggests something to do while you wait, and disappears
> when the task finishes. Free, MIT licensed, runs entirely on the local machine
> with no server and no account. The user interface is in Korean.

## What it is

Idle Buddy watches Claude Code and Codex through their hook systems. When a task
exceeds 30 seconds, a small mascot window appears in the bottom-right corner of the
screen and offers a quest: a mini game, a joke, a breathing exercise, or a short
chore. When the task completes, the mascot beeps and fades out. It never appears
while the user is typing.

- Platform: macOS only (Apple Silicon and Intel). Hooks run elsewhere, the mascot window does not.
- Requirements: Node.js 18 or later, and Claude Code or Codex (either one is enough).
- Rust is optional. Without it the installer downloads a prebuilt app from Releases.
- Install: `git clone https://github.com/delochy/idle-buddy.git && cd idle-buddy && sh install.sh`
- Uninstall: `node uninstall.js`
- License: MIT. Author: delochy.

## What you can do while waiting

- Ten mini games in the widget window: block stacking, sudoku, 2048, minesweeper, snake, whack-a-mole, tic-tac-toe, memory match, reaction time, typing practice.
- Around 100 developer jokes and 90 riddles, shown without repeats until the pool is exhausted.
- Ambient rest modes: campfire, ocean with sound, guided breathing, stretching.
- Chores that open the relevant app: shopping list, desktop and downloads cleanup, unanswered messages.

## Progression and reporting

- The mascot gains experience from time spent waiting and quests chosen. Levels unlock cosmetic items: ribbon, glasses, hat, crown.
- A daily waiting report shows time waited, number of long tasks, tokens consumed by Claude Code and Codex, and what was done while waiting. It exports as a 1080x1350 share image.
- Unfinished games and lists resume the next time the mascot appears.
- Claude Code and Codex can run at the same time; one window shows which agent is working.

## Privacy

No server and no account. All data stays in the repository's `data/` folder and is
never transmitted. Stored fields are task start and end times, the working
directory, the first 200 characters of the prompt, and the quest chosen. Typing
detection reads only the timestamp of the last keypress, never which key, so input
monitoring permission is not required. Token counts are read from the usage numbers
that Claude Code (`~/.claude/projects`) and Codex (`~/.codex/sessions`) already
write themselves.
